zh: 然后我认为你基本上需要把它框起来放到一边，然后说，这就是要在这里运作的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason you have to do that is because this can't change, right?
zh: 你必须这么做的原因是，因为这是不能变的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you can do secondaries, you can tweak it at the margin, but it's really, really hard to move a private book around.
zh: 我的意思是，你可以做 secondary（份额转让），你可以在边际上微调，但要移动一个私募账本真的是非常非常难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would your answer be for what sort of liquidity profile you thought you needed when you were considering this?
zh: 当你在考虑这个问题时，对于你认为需要什么样的流动性特征，你的答案会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our allocation range around privates is 35 to 55, which means that we want 55 to be the case when we have a denominator issue.
zh: 所以我们围绕私募的配置区间是 35 到 55，这意味着我们希望在出现分母问题的时候是 55。

speaker: Unknown
en: When equities have gone down and the public side is smaller than it usually is because of this particular difficulty in the market, that the private side isn't going to kick up so much that we're going to be forced into selling.
zh: 当股票下跌、公开市场那一侧因为市场的这种特定困难而比通常更小的时候，私募那一侧不会涨得太多，以至于我们被迫卖出。

speaker: Unknown
en: The number one thing to avoid is fraud, and the number two thing to avoid is forced selling.
zh: 头号要避免的事情是欺诈，二号要避免的事情是被迫卖出。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a disaster.
zh: 那是一场灾难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we kind of target 45%.
zh: 所以我们大致以 45% 为目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: If Publix race ahead, then it puts some downward pressure on that.
zh: 如果公开市场跑在前面，那会对其产生一些向下的压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we get into, you know, a financial crisis, something like that, it would put upward pressure on that.
zh: 而如果我们进入，你知道的，一场金融危机之类的情况，那会对其产生向上的压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for example, the last bit in 2022, when tech, you know, kind of slid a bunch, or you could go back a couple of years prior to the pandemic, I think that our private side got to like 51, 52.
zh: 但比如，最近的一次是在 2022 年，当科技股，你知道的，滑落了一大截的时候，或者你可以回到疫情前几年，我想我们的私募那一侧到了大概 51、52。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it wasn't so much that it either constrained our ability to allocate, and it certainly wasn't enough that we got into a forced selling situation.
zh: 但还没有多到限制我们的配置能力，而且当然也远没有到让我们陷入被迫卖出的境地。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you think about then the 45% say that we have as the ideal, drilling one layer blower, how do you think about how to split that up between venture, PE, and every other private that we can do?
zh: 当你考虑那 45% 这个我们所说的理想值时，往下再钻一层，你如何思考在风险投资、PE 以及其他所有可做的私募之间进行拆分？

speaker: Unknown
en: We've had a different perspective on this over the last five or six years that really came out of what I was talking about before when we knew that the school was going to have issues as it related to enrollment, right?
zh: 在过去五六年里，我们对此有一个不同的看法，它真正源于我之前谈到的那件事，当时我们知道学校在招生方面会遇到问题，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not just a Baylor thing, but like every school.
zh: 这不只是 Baylor 一家的事，而是每所学校都是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Demographics can kind of be a slow moving train wreck.
zh: 人口结构在某种程度上可能是一场缓慢发生的列车事故。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the benefit of the slow movement is that we can sit back and look five years out and know what's going to happen.
zh: 但缓慢移动的好处是，我们可以坐下来往五年后看，知道会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we started this five or six years ago, like shortly after the pandemic.
zh: 所以我们在五六年之前开始了这件事，大概是在疫情之后不久。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we basically said the single reason that privates exist is to make money.
zh: 而我们基本上说，私募存在的唯一理由就是赚钱。

en: Period.

speaker: Unknown
en: End of story.
zh: 故事结束。

en: And so anything in the private book that isn't going to lend itself to excess returns.
zh: 所以私募账本里任何不会带来超额回报的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, we need to create money to create more distributions for the school that's going to have enrollment concerns.
zh: 再说一遍，我们需要创造资金，为那个将面临招生问题的学校创造更多的分配。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're not going to keep up with the highest returns that we can generate out of the private book,
zh: 所以如果你跟不上我们能从私募账本里产生的最高回报，

speaker: Unknown
en: We've kind of moved on from that.
zh: 我们基本上已经从那里走开了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of the real asset stuff in our book is sort of like winding down, not being renewed.
zh: 所以我们账本里很多实物资产类的东西正在慢慢收缩，不再续投。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're really focusing, to get back to your question, today, we're focusing on VC, expansion, growth equity capital, and buyout.
zh: 所以回到你的问题,我们今天真正专注于的是 VC、扩张型、成长型股权资本和收购。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of it, right?
zh: 大概就是这样,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we're going to lock up money, we want the highest returns.
zh: 所以如果我们要锁定资金,我们就想要最高的回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about trying then, if you want VC, you want growth equity, how do you think about trying to get into the big names, the Sequoias, the Benchmarks, the Founders Funds, the you name those big brands versus trying to find the young upstart, the little boutique provider that could do a 10x?
zh: 那么你当时是怎么想的呢,如果你想要 VC,想要成长型股权,你怎么考虑挤进那些大名鼎鼎的机构,红杉、Benchmark、Founders Fund,你说的那些大品牌, versus 去寻找年轻的新秀,那种可能做到 10 倍的小精品机构?

speaker: Unknown
en: I will say that, you know, we're coming along a little bit later to the party than some of the Ivy Leagues or Stanford or what have you as it relates to the sort of like VC brand names that you're talking about.
zh: 我想说的是,你知道,在你说到的这些 VC 品牌名号方面,我们比一些常春藤或斯坦福之类的进场稍微晚了一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it hasn't been for lack of trying.
zh: 所以这不是没努力过。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just like when you knock on the door, they kind of like don't answer.

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've kind of had to go.

zh: 我们某种程度上不得不想办法用不同的方式解决这个问题。

en: What I will say, though, is that the ladies in our office have had exceptional, absolutely exceptional returns out of like the expansion growth equity category.
zh: 不过我想说的是,我们办公室的女士们在扩张型成长股权这个类别上获得了非常出色、绝对出色的回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've actually had, you know, some questions of like, should we just allocate more dollars to that sector of the market at the margin we have?
zh: 所以实际上我们有过一些讨论,比如,在边际上我们是不是应该把更多资金配置到市场的这个板块?

speaker: Unknown
en: But I would say we still do VC.
zh: 但我想说我们仍然做 VC。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still in probably newer upstarting names.
zh: 它大概仍然是较新的新兴名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: David, do you like VC?
zh: David,你喜欢 VC 吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I do.
zh: 我喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a little perplexed by the length of some of these funds.
zh: 不过说实话,我对这些基金的一些期限长度有点困惑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got to be honest, it's not clear to me that the GP incentives are aligned with the math that runs endowments.
zh: 我不确定 GP 的激励是否与捐赠基金运作的数学逻辑一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean?
zh: 这是什么意思?

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's just do it for example, right?
zh: 我们就直接举个例子,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, historically they were like 10, 12 year funds.
zh: 你知道,历史上它们大概是 10 年、12 年的基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now they're like 15, 18 year funds, right?
zh: 现在变成了 15 年、18 年的基金,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So much to the chagrin of like all LPs.
zh: 让所有 LP 都很懊恼。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the issue that you run into is that, okay, so you get your money back in 15 or 18 years and let's just say it was like phenomenal experience and you're up like 15X.
zh: 但你遇到的问题是,好,你在 15 年或 18 年后拿回你的钱,假设这是一次非常出色的经历,你赚了 15 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, that's fantastic.
zh: 你会觉得,那太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the issue is that it happened over 15 to 18 years.
zh: 但问题是它是在 15 到 18 年里发生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what simple math would suggest is that if you were in a growth equity fund that was six years in weighted average life, and you were up 3x, and then you redeployed into another growth equity fund that was up 3x in six years, and then you did it again, that over the course of 18 years, you'd be up 27x.
zh: 而简单的数学告诉我们,如果你投了一只加权平均存续期为 6 年的成长型股权基金,赚了 3 倍,然后你把资金重新投入另一只 6 年赚 3 倍的成长型股权基金,然后再来一次,那么在 18 年里,你会赚 27 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is better than 15x by like a factor of two.
zh: 这比 15 倍好,大概好了一倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I understand why people want to hang on to their winners.
zh: 所以我理解为什么人们想抓着他们的赢家不放。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the compounding of capital and I'm trying to create the largest pile of money for students.
zh: 但资本的复利——而我在努力为学生创造最大的一堆钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Students can't pay their tuition with returns.
zh: 学生不能用回报交学费。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to pay with dollars.
zh: 他们必须用美元来交。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm expressly interested in creating the largest pile of money.
zh: 所以我明确关心的是创造最大的一堆钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the largest pile of money is governed by like simple compounding math.
zh: 而最大的一堆钱是由简单的复利数学支配的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we're really after is the velocity of capital, not just returns on capital.
zh: 所以我们真正追求的是资本的速度,而不仅仅是资本回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whenever the velocity of capital is going to start to asymptotically approach like wherever it's going to be, then we want to be out and move on to the next thing.
zh: 每当资本的速度开始渐近地趋于它将要到达的那个水平时,我们就想退出,转向下一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, like it's really, really hard to do like 3X in six years, right?
zh: 换句话说,比如在六年里做到 3 倍,真的、真的很难,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easier.
zh: 更容易的方式是。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have winners now.
zh: 你现在有赢家了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The company's going okay.
zh: 公司运转得还不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually looks better on your marketing if you're up 6X instead of 3X.
zh: 如果你涨了 6 倍而不是 3 倍,你的市场营销看起来其实更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like if people held onto it for another five years and got like a double, then they'd be up 6X instead of 3X.
zh: 所以如果人们再持有它五年,拿到一个翻倍,那他们就是涨 6 倍而不是 3 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: That suggests that the next fund will be raised, et cetera, et cetera.
zh: 这意味着下一只基金就能募到,等等等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I actually don't care about any of that.
zh: 但说实话我一点都不在乎这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's a business decision.
zh: 那是一个商业决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's related to the business.
zh: 那是和业务相关的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm not optimizing for the best business for the GP.
zh: 而我不是在为 GP 的最佳业务做优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm trying to optimize for the biggest pile of money for our students.
zh: 我是在努力为我们的学生优化最大的一堆钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I get that there's a little bit of a disconnect there, but the math issue does kind of drive me nuts.
zh: 所以我知道这里面有点脱节,但这个数学问题确实让我有点抓狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I ask you a blunt question then?
zh: 那我能问你一个直白的问题吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I love this interview because it's completely not in my interest as a venture investor and as someone who interviews venture investors.
zh: 我喜欢这次访谈，因为作为一个风险投资人、也作为一个采访风险投资人的人，这完全不符合我的利益。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, this is why I love it.
zh: 不，不，这就是我喜欢它的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have the best job in the world.
zh: 我拥有世界上最好的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But given the requirements on velocity of cash and the value of compounding, which I very clearly see, do you not have a question internally of, well, why do VC at all?
zh: 但考虑到对资金周转速度的要求和复利价值——这些我看得很清楚——你们内部难道不会有这样的疑问：那为什么还要做风投呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: If we can do growth equity or mid-market and get the 3x in six years, I get you, David.
zh: 如果我们能做成长期股权或中型市场，六年后拿到 3 倍回报，我理解你，David。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not doing that for you.
zh: 我不会为你那么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And neither is the best firms.
zh: 最好的那些机构也不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is a question that gets batted around a lot in our office.
zh: 这是在我们办公室里被反复讨论的一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, there is something to be said about sort of laddering returns.
zh: 所以，你知道，关于回报的阶梯式安排，是有话可说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's OK to go allocate money to some manager and say, like, those returns are going to show up like six, seven, 10 years from now.
zh: 也就是说，你可以把钱配置给某个基金管理人，然后说，这些回报大概会在六年、七年、十年后才显现。

speaker: Unknown
en: These other returns are going to show up three to five years from now.
zh: 另外一些回报会在三到五年后显现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then kind of on my side, those returns are going to show up one to three years from now.
zh: 然后在我这一侧，这些回报会在一到三年后显现。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we do think about it that way.
zh: 所以我们确实是这么考虑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I would say that there's a rule in our office that you're not allowed to talk about returns without also talking about time.
zh: 但我要说，我们办公室有一条规则：谈论回报的时候，必须同时谈论时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it's very common on the private side to just say everything like, well, you're up 2x, 3x, 5x, whatever.
zh: 因为在私募这一侧，很常见的说法就是：哦，你翻了 2 倍、3 倍、5 倍，什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that tells you nothing.
zh: 但那什么都说明不了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're up 5x over 30 years, that's horrible.
zh: 如果你花 30 年翻了 5 倍，那很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're up 5x in five months, that's amazing.
zh: 如果你 5 个月翻了 5 倍，那太惊人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess that's SpaceX.
zh: 我猜那就是 SpaceX。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is Venture then just a pure diversification play for you?
zh: 那么风投对你来说纯粹就是一种分散化配置吗？

en: It is for us.
zh: 对我们来说是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it is.
zh: 是的，是的。

en: It could be the case that somebody allocates to something that really takes off and goes quite well.

en: Like, for example, we happen to have about two and a half percent of the endowment in Anthropic.

en: We have no exposure to SpaceX.
zh: 我们没有 SpaceX 的敞口。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well done.
zh: 干得漂亮。

en: David, for goodness sake, will you please learn from your managers, okay?
zh: David，看在老天的份上，请你向你的基金管理人学习，好吗？

en: Lesson number one of venture capital, even if it was not you, you take credit and say thank you so much.
zh: 风投的第一课：就算不是你的功劳，你也要揽下荣誉，说一声非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember that one, yes.
zh: 我记得那一条，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not really how we roll at Baylor, but understood.
zh: 那不太是 Baylor 的行事风格，但明白了。

en: Can I ask you, it's a really different, and I'm not saying with Anthropic here, but I'm saying with positions that go public, Anthropic obviously will be one, but with positions that go public in the past, how do you think about the, I'm going to actively manage it as now the holder versus a common one that I hear, which is, that's not our job.
zh: 我能问你一个问题吗，这是一个很不一样的——我不是说 Anthropic 这里，我是说上市了的持仓，Anthropic 显然会是其中之一——但对于过去上市了的持仓，你怎么看待：一种是像我这样，作为持有人现在主动管理它；另一种是我常听到的说法：那不是我们的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just liquidate the minute that we get it because we don't know about this asset.
zh: 我们一拿到就立刻清仓，因为我们不了解这个资产。

en: How do you think about it?
zh: 你怎么看待这个问题？

zh: 也取决于它上市后持仓的规模。

en: We've also had shares before.
zh: 我们以前也持有过股票。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it kind of depends to us what we're expecting, what the profile of the portfolio looks like, and the position and the risk associated with it.
zh: 所以对我们来说，这取决于我们的预期、投资组合的整体画像，以及这个持仓及其相关风险。

zh: 那个吗，是我写下来的原因吗？

en: Can you talk to me about that, your process there, what you saw that others didn't and how you thought about that?
zh: 能跟我讲讲那件事吗，你那边的流程，你看到了别人没看到什么，以及你是怎么思考的？

en: I'm just fascinated given that.

en: I would say, like, if we had an edge, I would say that we're pretty good on human behavior.

en: And so a lot of these things, you know, I don't dispute at all.

zh: 比如，我不是工程师。

en: Much of the stuff that comes out of Silicon Valley is over my head.
zh: 硅谷产出的很多东西都超出了我的理解范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do know how people think and I do know how people make decisions.
zh: 但我确实知道人们怎么思考，也确实知道人们怎么做决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was pretty easy in this case of, you know, like software is dead.
zh: 所以在这个案例里就挺容易的，你知道，比如“软件已死”。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all going to zero.
zh: 一切都要归零了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Somebody is going to vibe code this and whatever.
zh: 有人会去 vibe coding 这些什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, I have friends that run three, 500 person private family businesses.
zh: 而比如，我有一些朋友经营着三家、500人的私人家族企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's easy enough to pick up the phone, call them.
zh: 打个电话给他们很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're like, hey, say your son-in-law vibe codes something and you're going to like tear out your CRM.
zh: 我们就说，嘿，比如说你女婿用 vibe coding 搞了个东西，然后你要把你的 CRM 拆掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're like, not in a million years.
zh: 他们说，绝对不会，一百万年也不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not their job.
zh: 那不是他们的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I have a good friend who runs like a vertically integrated like potpourri business.
zh: 比如我有个好朋友，经营着一个垂直整合的香薰企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: He knows everything that there is to know about that, but he is not going to tear out key important parts of what makes his business run behind the scenes on some unproven thing that I think it was the CEO of Salesforce, like, I don't know, six or eight months ago said that like the best that AI was gonna be is like 93% right, which is like phenomenal.
zh: 他对这一行无所不知，但他不会把让他的业务后台运转的关键部分拆掉换到某个未经证实的东西上——我记得好像是 Salesforce 的 CEO，大概六八个月前说过，AI 最好的程度也就是大约 93% 的正确率，而这已经很惊人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that might be like better than like a lot of people, but the issue of software is 100% right.
zh: 那可能比很多人类强，但问题在于软件是 100% 正确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you need your books to like match up and whatever, like, yeah, that's not going to happen.
zh: 所以如果你需要你的账目能对得上之类的，那，是的，那不会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I actually think as we've kind of like thought about it more, I actually think that in some of these vertical industries, that software is actually going to be the delivery mechanism for AI.
zh: 所以实际上，随着我们更多地思考，我实际上认为在一些垂直行业里，软件反而会成为 AI 的交付机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, for my friend who's in a niche business, very, very good at what they do, I think they're the only vertically integrated potpourri maker in the world.
zh: 换句话说，对于我这个做利基生意、非常非常擅长自己业务的朋友——我认为他们是世界上唯一的垂直整合香薰制造商——

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that what's going to happen is that the trust that's been built up with the software providers
zh: 我认为将会发生的是，与软件提供商之间建立起来的信任

speaker: Unknown
en: is going to translate into, hey, could you add AI bits for me on the back of this software?
zh: 会转化为，嘿，能不能在这套软件的基础上帮我加上 AI 的部分？

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, like the SaaS companies aren't stupid.
zh: 而且，当然，SaaS 公司不傻。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like they're sitting there and like, hey, we're worth, you know, 20 or $50 billion.
zh: 他们不是坐在那里说，嘿，我们价值，你知道，200 或 500 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should let this go to zero.
zh: 我们应该让这一切归零。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's interesting for me is you analyze this situation and then you decide to act on it.
zh: 对我来说有意思的是，你分析这个情况，然后决定据此行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like this is very rare for an institution to do normally.
zh: 像这种做法，对一家机构来说通常是非常罕见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sean and others have like told me that, but like that I don't actually understand, right?
zh: Sean 和其他人跟我这么说过，但我其实不理解，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because like software at that point is like on sale to the tune of like 50, 60% from like October of 25.
zh: 因为那时候软件相当于打了对折还多，比如相比 25 年 10 月跌了 50%、60%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if the thesis is software is going away, it's down 50, 60%, you call businesses and they say, that's not true.
zh: 而且如果论点是软件要消亡了，它跌了 50%、60%，你打电话给企业，他们说，那不是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, I'll own that.
zh: 你会说，我认。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get you, but it's throwing the baby out with the bathwater.
zh: 我理解你，但这是把孩子和洗澡水一起倒掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The trouble is, I'm not sure what's the baby and I'm not sure what's the bathwater.
zh: 麻烦在于，我不确定什么是孩子，我也不确定什么是洗澡水。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with the greatest of respects, I live in technology.
zh: 而且恕我直言，我是活在技术圈里的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why we have managers like Sean, right?
zh: 这就是为什么我们有像 Sean 这样的经理人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's the expert.
zh: 所以他是专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm like, I'm going to give you more money, but I want you to go through your list with me and tell me all the things that are least likely to be interdicted by AI and then like own those.
zh: 所以我说，我会给你更多钱，但我要你跟我一起过一遍你的清单，告诉我所有最不可能被 AI 干掉的东西，然后就重仓持有那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm making a decision based on human behavior and how I know people make decisions, right?
zh: 所以我是基于人类行为和我所知的人们的决策方式在做决策，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm allocating based on that.
zh: 然后我据此进行配置。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm relying on the manager to be expert in their individual field and give me the correct perspective and what's going on on the ground.
zh: 但我依赖经理人成为他们各自领域的专家，给我正确的视角和地面上实际发生的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what's so interesting is most just delegate to managers and go, you're the experts.
zh: 但有意思的是，大多数人只是委托给经理人，说，你是专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: You delegate to them, great.
zh: 你委托给他们，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you go, I'm also going to operate where I have decisions myself, and I'm going to interject in those markets.
zh: 然后你还会说，我自己也会在有决策权的领域行动，我会在那些市场里介入。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's different.
zh: 这不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I kind of think that that's our job, right?
zh: 我有点觉得这就是我们的工作，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, like my seed is like an allocator seed.
zh: 我是说，比如我的 seed 就像一个配置型 seed。

speaker: Unknown
en: My job is to allocate.
zh: 我的职责就是配置。

speaker: Unknown
en: To go back to the like the Buffett or Charlie example, right?
zh: 回到那个巴菲特或 Charlie 的例子，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They also are allocators and they're deciding who gets the incremental dollars.
zh: 他们也是配置者，他们在决定增量资金给谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they send it to Burlington Northern or do they send it to their energy company?
zh: 是投给 Burlington Northern，还是投给他们的能源公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: And depending on what the outlook is, what the CapEx requirements are, et cetera, you know, they get budgets submitted to them and they may or may not allocate more of their cash pile to those companies.
zh: 取决于前景如何、资本开支要求是什么等等，你知道，预算会提交给他们，他们可能会也可能不会把更多现金储备配置给那些公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Quite a lot of LPs that I speak to say, I get the liquidity challenge of venture and I get the time lags of venture being difficult, but I learn a lot from what happens in my venture portfolios in terms of AI penetration, new technologies, adoption cycles.
zh: 我交谈过的很多 LP 都说，我理解风投的流动性挑战，也理解风投的时间滞后很困难，但我从我的风投组合中能学到很多，比如 AI 渗透、新技术、采纳周期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is your venture portfolio a learning academy for you or not?
zh: 你的风投组合对你来说是不是一个学习学院？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not for me.
zh: 对我不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say it goes the other way.
zh: 我觉得方向是反过来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually learn a lot from the public side managers.
zh: 我实际上从公募侧的经理人那里学到很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I find is that there's a lot of this spun up like, oh my gosh, we're gonna have autonomous cars in like three years in 2016.
zh: 我发现有很多这种被吹起来的东西，比如 2016 年的时候那种“天哪，我们三年内就会有自动驾驶汽车了”。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, right.
zh: 是吧，对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like all the regulatory stuff that you have to go through so that you don't kill somebody.
zh: 就是你得通过的所有监管流程，免得撞死人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we're 10 years on and what do we have like 5,000 cars on the road?
zh: 对啊，十年过去了，我们现在路上有多少？大概 5000 辆车？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, please.
zh: 拜托。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like, I get sort of like the mental imagination that, you know, you can go like, we could put something on the moon and we could mine the moon and whatever.
zh: 所以我理解那种思维想象力，你可以想说，我们可以把东西放上月球，我们可以开采月球，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like get back to me in 30 years.
zh: 三十年后再来找我吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, but do you not worry then about the casinoization of public markets?
zh: 好吧，但你不担心公开市场的赌场化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不担心。

speaker: Unknown
en: The public markets are the big leagues.
zh: 公开市场是大联盟。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's millions of people making decisions on dollars every single day for every single company.
zh: 每一天，每一家公司，都有数百万人在用真金白银做决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know how things get valued on the private side?
zh: 你知道私募侧的东西是怎么估值的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course you do.
zh: 你当然知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Three people get in the room and say, hey, I think the value is X.
zh: 三个人进一个房间说，嘿，我觉得价值是 X。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're like, I'll fund it at that.
zh: 然后他们说，我就按这个价投。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that resets the whole price.
zh: 这样整个价格就被重设了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think public markets in many respects are as irrational as private markets are today.
zh: 但我认为如今的公开市场在很多方面和私募市场一样不理性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you saw that.
zh: 你也看到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dude, you saw that.
zh: 老兄，你是看到了的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You saw that with the state.
zh: 你在那件事上看到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can be irrational because they are governed by people.
zh: 它们会不理性，因为它们是由人主导的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The difference is that there are tens of millions of people trading on that information, whereas on the private side, there's like three.
zh: 区别在于，有几千万人基于那些信息交易，而在私募侧，大概只有三个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they decided, those tens of millions of people, that Elon Musk is a premium in himself, that SpaceX should be a $1.8 trillion business.
zh: 而那几千万人决定了，Elon Musk 本身就是一种溢价，SpaceX 应该是一家 1.8 万亿美元的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: That doesn't mean that they're right.
zh: 这不代表他们是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just means that it incorporates all available information, which does not happen on the private side.
zh: 只是意味着它纳入了所有可获得的信息，而私募侧不会发生这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what you're saying is that the sheer scale of people voting in this buying decision means that it's a more legitimate price than private side, just so I understand.
zh: 所以你的意思是，在这个买入决策中投票的人的庞大规模意味着它比私募侧的价格更正当，我只是确认一下理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Correct.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think there's any question about that.
zh: 我觉得这一点毫无疑问。

speaker: Unknown
en: I literally have been in these conversations, right, where like three guys get together and are like, hey, I think it should be this.
zh: 我真的亲身经历过这类对话，就是三个人凑在一起说，嘿，我觉得它应该值这个数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, on what, right?
zh: 我会问，凭什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, well, I'll give you $50 million at that price.
zh: 然后我们说，嗯，我按那个价给你 5000 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, fine.
zh: 好，行。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the fact that I tried the product and I liked it, David, why are you asking me such intellectual questions?
zh: 凭我试用了产品并且我喜欢，David，你为什么问我这么有智力含量的问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 正是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you trust, and I didn't mean that badly, but do you trust the prices coming back from your managers?
zh: 那你信任吗——我不是恶意——你信任你的经理人报回来的价格吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we all have our books, our portfolios for people listening, and we mark them in different ways.
zh: 你知道，对于听众来说，我们都有自己的账本、自己的组合，我们用不同的方式做估值标记。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do.
zh: 确实是。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one thing that the ladies have done extremely good job of.
zh: 所以这一点上那些女士们做得非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: Recall, again, that I'm coming from the public side.
zh: 再提醒一下，我是从公募侧过来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you run trading books, everything has to be priced every day, right?
zh: 所以当你管理交易账本时，一切都必须每天定价，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So ostensibly it's so you make better decisions because if you have things mismarked, then psychology works against you.
zh: 名义上这是为了让你做出更好的决策，因为如果你的资产标记错了，心理就会跟你作对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you say that this is worth $30 million and it should be worth $10 million,
zh: 比如你说这个东西值 3000 万美元,但它应该只值 1000 万美元,

speaker: Unknown
en: And somebody offers you 20, then because you would ostensibly take a loss from 30 to 20, you're liable not to hit that, even though it's a premium to the actual value.
zh: 然后有人出价 2000 万,那么因为你名义上会从 3000 万亏损到 2000 万,你可能就得为没达到那个数字负责,即使相对于实际价值来说那是溢价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so pricing is just a way to make sure that you are psychologically aligned to the reality of the market.
zh: 所以定价只是一种确保你在心理上与市场现实保持一致的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of the things that we really try to do is to make sure that our managers are not pushing valuations.
zh: 因此我们真正努力做的事情之一,就是确保我们的基金经理不去推高估值。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want valuations to be conservative rather than aggressive.
zh: 我们希望估值偏保守而不是偏激进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see that in sort of our return data in sort of like the six months, nine months prior to something being taken out.
zh: 你可以在我们的回报数据中看到这一点,大致是在某个项目退出前的六到九个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think average gain on that is sort of like 60 to 90 percent.
zh: 我认为那期间的平均涨幅大约是 60% 到 90%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think from a market perspective, it's more like 30 to 50 percent.
zh: 而从市场角度来看,大概是 30% 到 50%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which would suggest that our marks, our managers' marks, tend to be more conservative than others.
zh: 这说明我们的估值标记,我们基金经理的估值标记,往往比其他人更保守。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, like I kind of sit on top of this thing and I kind of have to vouch for the valuations that we have as it relates to talking to the regents or administration.
zh: 所以,你知道,我有点像是坐在这个东西的顶端,在跟校董会或校方管理层沟通时,我得为我们持有的估值做担保。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel pretty comfortable that on the private side, our marks are actually more sane than on average.
zh: 而我相当有信心,在私募这边,我们的估值标记实际上比平均水平更合理。

speaker: Unknown
en: As venture eats more and more of the world with your OpenAI, your Anthropics, your SpaceX, your biggest companies in the world all being venture-backed companies, do you maybe feel that you need more in venture, more in tech?
zh: 随着风险投资越来越多地吞噬这个世界,你的 OpenAI、你的 Anthropics、你的 SpaceX,世界上最大的公司全都是风险投资支持的公司,你会不会觉得你需要配置更多到风险投资、更多到科技?

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it change how you view the world?
zh: 这会改变你看世界的方式吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Does the mindset change?
zh: 心态会变吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I feel pretty comfortable with where we stand.
zh: 不会,我对我们目前的立场相当有信心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think our biggest allocation is in growth equity on the private side.
zh: 我认为我们在私募方面最大的配置是在成长型股权。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we feel pretty comfortable with our capability and the manager set that we have there.
zh: 而且我们对我们在那块的能力和基金经理阵容感到相当有信心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you like growth equity?
zh: 你为什么喜欢成长型股权?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because of the return to timeline profile?
zh: 是因为回报与时间线的特征吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: The return timeline, there's also fewer zeros.
zh: 回报时间线,而且归零的更少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that kind of goes to the value bit.
zh: 所以这就回到了价值那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's just simple math.
zh: 我是说,这就是简单的数学。

speaker: Unknown
en: If there are fewer zeros, then everything else doesn't have to cover for the things that don't work, which is what helps get you to, like, I think that their book is like...
zh: 如果归零的更少,那么其他部分就不必为那些不成功的项目买单,这正是能让你达到——比如,我认为他们的账本是像……

speaker: Unknown
en: Annualizing it like 30% on sort of like the growth equity side.
zh: 在成长型股权这边年化大约 30%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that obviously meets our eight, 9% bogey.
zh: 所以这显然达到了我们 8%、9% 的目标线。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't even actually know that I've ever had that question before.
zh: 所以我其实都不记得以前被问过这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about like Mulligan vintages across Venture and P, Mulligan being like not very good vintages?
zh: 你怎么看待风险投资和 P 里的 Mulligan 年份?Mulligan 就是指不太好的年份?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, a lot of people are talking about kind of 21, 22 for Venture and P being just like very bad vintages.
zh: 你知道,很多人都在谈论风险投资和 P 的 21、22 年是非常糟糕的年份。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all just kind of went crazy.
zh: 我们当时都有点疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was COVID, sorry, mea culpa.
zh: 那是 COVID,抱歉,我的错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you've got now Toma Bravo, obviously, who had Medallia, which is obviously quite a well-known return, the key situation.
zh: 然后现在你有 Toma Bravo,显然,他们有 Medallia,那显然是一个相当有名的、回报关键的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that just kind of comes with the territory, right?
zh: 我认为这本来就是这一行的一部分,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, like, basically what we do is we say, this is the amount that's going to be in privates.
zh: 我是说,基本上我们做的就是:我们说,这是配置到私募的金额。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we say, we're going to allocate to PE expansion capital in VC, and we're going to do it in these sectors.
zh: 然后我们说,我们要配置到 PE、扩张型资本和 VC,我们要在这些板块里做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I let the ladies have at it.
zh: 然后我就让女士们放手去干。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they come up with a portfolio and the portfolio overall has sort of an expected return hurdle that they need to clear.
zh: 然后她们拿出一个投资组合,而这个组合整体上有一个需要达到的预期回报门槛。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they're not clearing it, then that's a problem.
zh: 如果她们没达到,那就是个问题。

en: So do you think your colleagues are nuts then for not hiring internally?
zh: 那么你觉得你的同行们不内部招人（培养）就是疯了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that nuts is not the word that I would use.
zh: 我觉得「疯」不是我會用的词。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say that they are accepting alternative risks.
zh: 我会说他们是在接受另一种风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the alternative risks are on the upside to me is that I have a stable team.
zh: 这种另一种风险，对我而言好处是我有一支稳定的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I have worked with Renee for almost 16 years.
zh: 我和 Renee 共事快 16 年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next person that we hired, Jen, she's been here 11 years.
zh: 我们招的下一个人，Jen，她在这里 11 年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can like kind of go on down the line.
zh: 然后你可以这样一路数下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: That actually accrues, is pretty evident across the industry.
zh: 这实际上是会累积的，在整个行业里相当明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like longevity begets returns.
zh: 就是长久性带来回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm benefited on the stability front.
zh: 所以我在稳定性这方面是受益的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The negative for me is that the upfront bearing of all of that time, there's a period of time where I have to like carry the team.
zh: 对我的坏处是，前期要承担所有那些时间投入，有一段时间我必须扛着整个团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the flip side, if you hire mid-career professionals,
zh: 反过来说，如果你招职业生涯中期的专业人士，

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have sort of like that upfront cost of like having to carry the team, right?
zh: 你就没有那种前期要扛团队的成本，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they're more plug and play, but you sort of wear this risk of turnover and potentially or returns.
zh: 因为他们更即插即用，但你承担的是人员流动的风险，以及潜在的回报风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: David, do you think the incentive structure for LPs is broken?
zh: David，你觉得 LP 的激励结构坏掉了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And let's be specific on LPs or endowment fund investors.
zh: 让我们具体说 LP 或者说捐赠基金投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at funder funds, if I crush it for my funder funds, they obviously have carry and they will do very well from that.
zh: 如果你看基金中的基金，如果我为我的基金中的基金做得特别出色，他们显然有 carry，会从中赚得非常多。

speaker: Unknown
en: With traditional endowment fund investing,
zh: 而传统的捐赠基金投资，

speaker: Unknown
en: If I do really well for you, it doesn't necessarily translate to a huge paycheck.
zh: 如果我为你做得非常好，这不一定转化成一份高额的薪水。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do we have a wrong incentive mechanism?
zh: 我们是不是有一个错误的激励机制？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it's a wrong incentive mechanism.
zh: 我不认为这是一个错误的激励机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that it requires people in the space to be very missional.
zh: 我认为这个行业的人必须有很强的使命感。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like I wake up every morning motivated by sending some sophomore in high school to Baylor that hasn't even thought about college yet.
zh: 就像我每天早上醒来，动力来自送某个还没考虑过上大学的高二学生去 Baylor。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or some like seventh or eighth grader who doesn't know if they're going to go to college and they're thinking about baseball scores from the prior night, right?
zh: 或者是某个七年级或八年级的孩子，还不知道自己会不会上大学，脑子里想的是前一晚的棒球比分，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like me getting out of bed in the morning, going to work and wanting to crush it is entirely due to that.
zh: 我每天早上起床、去工作、想要大干一场，完全是出于这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everyone likes to be able to get their wife something nice or to redo the kitchen in their house or go on trips.
zh: 每个人都喜欢能给妻子买点好东西，或者重新装修家里的厨房，或者去旅行。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like that is not the motivating factor for either myself or the people on my team.
zh: 但那不是我自己或者我团队成员的动力来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you worry about the impact of AI on education?
zh: 你担心 AI 对教育的影响吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I worry about the impact of AI on human thinking.
zh: 我担心的是 AI 对人类思考的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a number of studies out, I don't know about their veracity, but they're coming out of MIT and austere places like that that suggest that students who are using AI for everything that they do actually show less brain function, right?
zh: 现在有不少研究出炉，我不清楚它们的真实性如何，但它们来自 MIT 和 austere 那样的地方，表明那些做什么都用 AI 的学生实际上大脑功能表现更差，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this isn't really a surprise.
zh: 这其实并不奇怪。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see the same thing like if you just sit in a chair all day.
zh: 同样的道理，如果你整天坐在椅子上不动。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's your muscle atrophies.
zh: 你的肌肉会萎缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I do have concern about the effect of AI on actual human logic thinking.
zh: 所以我确实担心 AI 对人类真正的逻辑思考的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's sort of like an innately human trait.
zh: 这有点像是人类天生就有的特质。

speaker: Unknown
en: Animals don't think, humans think.
zh: 动物不会思考，人类会思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you abdicate your responsibility for thinking, it's not clear that humans do that either.
zh: 但如果你放弃了自己思考的责任，那人类还能不能思考就不确定了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I have concerns about that.
zh: 所以我对此有担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think education can figure it out and use it beneficially.
zh: 我认为教育可以解决这个问题，并有益地利用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's more of a human discipline problem.
zh: 我认为这更多是一个人类的自律问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a lot of my friends, CIOs of other endowments, sometimes larger, they've been hit with obviously the endowment fund tax, which is really hitting larger organizations.
zh: 对我的很多朋友来说，他们是其他捐赠基金——有时规模更大——的 CIO，他们明显受到了捐赠基金税的冲击，这个税主要打击的是规模更大的机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about that?
zh: 你怎么看这个问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you advise them?
zh: 你会怎么建议他们？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would love to be in their position.
zh: 我倒很乐意处在他们的位置上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are not because our endowment per student is too small to be subject to that.
zh: 我们没有，因为我们的生均捐赠基金规模太小，不适用那个税。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I promise you, if I went to the president of Baylor, I've actually had this conversation with Linda.
zh: 但我向你保证，如果我去找 Baylor 的校长——我实际上和 Linda 谈过这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I go to Linda and say like, there's good news and there's bad news.
zh: 如果我去找 Linda 说，有个好消息和一个坏消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bad news is that we're gonna have to pay an endowment tax.
zh: 坏消息是我们得交捐赠基金税了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The good news is that our endowment is three times bigger than when I last talked to you.
zh: 好消息是我们的捐赠基金比上次跟你谈话时大了三倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: She'd be like, yeah, and?
zh: 她会说，是吗，然后呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would love to have to pay the endowment tax because the endowment was bigger.
zh: 所以我倒很乐意交捐赠基金税，因为那意味着捐赠基金更大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you play a game of comparison?
zh: 你玩比较游戏吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it comparison is the thief of joy?
zh: 那句话怎么说来着——比较是快乐的小偷？

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, I think you said earlier in down times, you obviously are brilliant and in up times more challenging.
zh: 而且，你知道，我记得你之前说过，在下行时期，你显然很出色，而在上行时期更具挑战性。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you play a defensive game, full year 2025, Baylor return 9.4%, Dartmouth lowest 10.8%.
zh: 我想你打的是防守战，2025 全年，Baylor 回报 9.4%，Dartmouth 最低 10.8%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you do the comparative side by side or do you row your own race?
zh: 你会做横向比较，还是只划好自己的船？

speaker: Unknown
en: We do both, which I think is the right way to do it.
zh: 我们两者都做，我认为这才是正确的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every school has a different set of priorities, needs, et cetera.
zh: 每所学校都有不同的优先事项、需求等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Baylor's is currently to get the endowment higher on a per student basis.
zh: Baylor 目前的是要提高生均捐赠基金规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, for example, what you're referring to in terms of last year, that was disappointing on sort of like a relative basis.
zh: 所以，比如你提到的去年的情况，从相对的角度来看确实令人失望。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there were two bits that were going on.
zh: 但当时有两件事在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: One was that we had increased the allocation to privates by in sort of like annual commitment amount by about 60, 70% in 2020, 2021 and following.
zh: 一是我们把私募部分的配置——按年度承诺金额计算——在 2020、2021 年及其后提高了大约 60%、70%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so returns from the private side have been dealing with sort of like a second J curve, if you will.
zh: 所以私募那边的回报一直在经历所谓的第二条 J 曲线，可以这么说。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the funds of one, and then there's like another asset class that we had allocated to, those have been like flat and starting to inflect up.
zh: 然后是 fund of one，另外还有一个我们配置过的资产类别，那些一直很平，现在开始向上拐了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this fiscal year was the first year that we weren't dealing with the J curve impact on the private side.
zh: 所以这个财年是我们第一次不用再应对私募那边的 J 曲线影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the first year that we got returns from both, you know, the fund of one category and this other category,
zh: 也是第一年我们同时从两个类别——fund of one 类别和这个其他类别——获得了回报，

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we feel very, very good about sort of like, you know, our newest analyst was like, so basically you guys tried to change the engine while the car was moving.
zh: 所以我们感觉非常非常好，你知道，我们最新来的分析师说过，基本上你们就是在汽车行驶的时候换引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, that's 100% what we were trying to do.
zh: 是的，那 100% 就是我们想做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were trying to put a new, bigger engine in the car while it was still going down the highway.
zh: 我们就是想在车还在高速公路上跑的时候，给它装一个更大的新引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we did it.
zh: 而我们做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had like a little bit of a lag last year.
zh: 我们去年有一点滞后。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we'll be 18.5%, 19% this year without any SpaceX or Cerebrus or anything like that.
zh: 我觉得今年会是 18.5%、19%,不含 SpaceX 或 Cerebrus 之类的任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So structurally, I think the next couple of years look pretty good from sort of a tailwind perspective.
zh: 所以从结构上来说，从顺风的角度看，未来几年我觉得相当不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I ask you, we chatted before about a friend of mine who you're going to be working with.
zh: 我能问你吗，我们之前聊过我的一位朋友，你将要和他合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about position sizing in the positions that you do decide to engage with?
zh: 对于你决定参与的那些仓位，你是怎么考虑仓位规模的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is an interesting one.
zh: 这个问题很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're talking specifically on the private side.
zh: 你说的是专门针对私募这一边的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We spent a lot of time on this sort of because of what I had talked about earlier that like we own everything under the sun.
zh: 我们在这上面花了很多时间，因为我之前提到过，我们什么资产都持有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that we had figured out is that, yeah, you know, we have this relationship with GP and we have this, you know, they send us a little note.
zh: 而我们弄清楚的一件事是，是的，你知道，我们和 GP 有这种关系，我们有这种，你知道，他们给我们发个小通知。

speaker: Unknown
en: So and so company got sold.
zh: 某某公司被卖掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like a seven X return.
zh: 是七倍的回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, OK, great.
zh: 我就说，好的，很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean to us?
zh: 这对我们意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're like.
zh: 然后他们说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we'll get back like $400,000.
zh: 嗯，我们能拿回大概 40 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, what?
zh: 我就说，什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who cares?
zh: 谁在乎啊？

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it means nothing to the overall endowment.
zh: 这对整个捐赠基金来说什么都不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of the things that we've changed in sort of sizing is we start with how much money do we want to have in each underlying company?
zh: 所以我们在规模方面做出的一个改变是，我们从“我们想在每家底层公司里有多少钱”开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in other words, if the company is gonna be up 5X, we want that 5X to matter to the overall fund.
zh: 换句话说，如果这家公司要涨 5 倍，我们希望这 5 倍对整个基金有意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically what we're doing in sort of like expansion, buyout, venture's like a little bit of a different thing because it's a bigger company set.
zh: 所以基本上我们在成长、并购、风险投资方面做的事，风险投资有点不同，因为它是一家更大的公司集合。

speaker: Unknown
en: But basically what we're saying is we want $3 million to be in each underlying company.
zh: 但基本上我们说的是，我们希望每家底层公司里有 300 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if they have 10 companies on their platform, that means we'll allocate $30 million.
zh: 所以如果他们的平台上有 10 家公司，那就意味着我们会配置 3000 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get you totally.
zh: 我完全明白了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or another way that I think about it, and you can tell me if I'm wrong, which very possibly could be the case, I'm a low IQ individual after all, is it's a $200 million fund and you commit $20 million to it with the theory that if they say we are 10% ownership in every company, great.
zh: 或者我可以这样想，如果我错了你可以纠正我，这完全有可能，毕竟我是个低智商的人，就是一个 2 亿美元的基金，你承诺 2000 万美元，基于这样一个理论：如果他们说我们在每家公司都占 10%,那很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we're 10% of their fund, our exposure is 1% per company.
zh: 如果我们占他们基金的 10%,我们在每家公司的敞口就是 1%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we think about it in terms of dollars.
zh: 是的，我们是用美元来考虑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we say, how many companies are you gonna have?
zh: 所以我们会问，你们会有多少家公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: Eight, 10, 12?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we want two and a half to $3 million in each company.
zh: 然后我们希望每家公司里有 250 万到 300 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, it's up to the manager, you know, et cetera.
zh: 显然，这取决于基金经理，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not dictating that.
zh: 我们不会规定这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we're just doing the math from a dollars perspective.
zh: 我们只是从美元的角度做数学。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you have 10 companies, we want $3 million in each company.
zh: 所以如果你有 10 家公司，我们希望每家公司里有 300 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if it was up 5X, we'd get $15 million back.
zh: 这样如果涨了 5 倍，我们能拿回 1500 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: That matters.
zh: 这就有意义了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's enough to matter.
zh: 这足够有意义了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want your manager to do what they said they'd do or to play the game on the field?
zh: 你是希望你的基金经理按他们说的做，还是在场上随机应变？

speaker: Unknown
en: Ventures change more in a year than I've seen in a decade.
zh: 风险投资一年里的变化比我过去十年看到的还多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually playing the game on the field, as Bill Gurley says, is the job of a venture investor.
zh: 而且，正如 Bill Gurley 所说，在场上随机应变本来就是风险投资人的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: That may be different from what I said to you at our do.
zh: 这可能和我在我们的 do 上跟你说的不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We always want managers to do what they said that they were going to do.
zh: 我们一直希望基金经理按他们说过要做的方式去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like my example is always this.
zh: 我的例子总是这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I sort of view my job as like the general manager on a baseball team, right?
zh: 我有点把自己的工作看成棒球队的总经理，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to hire a third baseman, a shortstop, a second baseman, first baseman, et cetera, for various reasons, like depending on your fielding percentage, your batting average, et cetera.
zh: 所以我会出于各种原因雇佣一个三垒手、游击手、二垒手、一垒手等等，比如根据你的守备率、打击率等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if I walk out on the field and I have two people on second base, someone's getting fired.
zh: 但如果我走到场上，发现有两个人站在二垒上，有人要被解雇了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's probably the third baseman who switched to playing second because like I have people set up on the field to play particular roles for particular reasons.
zh: 而且很可能是那个改去打二垒的三垒手，因为我安排场上的人是为了特定的原因担任特定的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like if you're a third baseman and you think you can play second base better than my second baseman, then you should come talk to me.
zh: 所以，比如说，你是一个三垒手，你觉得你打二垒会比我现在的二垒手打得更好，那你就应该来找我谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if I ever walk out on the field and I have two second baseman and no third baseman, the third baseman is getting fired like full stop, right?
zh: 但如果我哪天走到球场上，发现有两个二垒手、没有一个三垒手，那个三垒手就会被开除，就是这样，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that I like I don't care what your returns are.
zh: 就是说，我不在乎你的回报是多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, we started off by talking about this.
zh: 所以，回到我们一开始聊的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We spend much more time on asset allocation and why things are where they are than we do on individual managers.
zh: 我们在资产配置以及“东西为什么在那里”上花的时间，比在个别基金经理身上花的时间多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, this is so interesting for me.
zh: 好，这对我来说太有意思了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the markets have changed in the time that I've raised from you.
zh: 所以，在我从你们这里募资的这段时间里，市场发生了变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've moved with those markets and I've done that well, and I'm showing you great numbers.
zh: 我用公开股票上更容易的事情来举例。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm making you money, but my position- If it doesn't fit what we're trying to accomplish, we won't re-up.
zh: 我在给你赚钱，但我的仓位——如果不符合我们想达成的东西，我们不会追加投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's so interesting.
zh: 这太有意思了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you would rather I stayed on second base, do worse financially than move to third base where you've already got someone else?
zh: 所以你宁可让我留在二垒、财务上做得更差，也不让我转到你已经有了别人的三垒？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would like you to have a conversation with me before you change your stripes.
zh: 我希望你是在改变路线之前，先和我谈一谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you say in that conversation?
zh: 在那次谈话里你会说什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd be like, why do you think that you should be able to do this when we have no data to suggest that you're good at this?
zh: 我会说：我们没有任何数据表明你擅长这件事，你凭什么认为自己能做到？

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's move out of VC.
zh: 我们跳出 VC 来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me do something on public equity that's easier.
zh: 让我做点公募股票方面更容易的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are managers who are like, we don't know how to time allocations into and out of cash.
